correctness.rationale: For every complex Hermitian positive-definite \(2\times2\) pair, positive determinant normalization preserves both curves up to a common scalar. The determinant-one square-root identity gives \(M=(A^{-1}+B)/K\) and \(N=(A^{-1}+D)/K\), equal determinants, and \(\operatorname{tr}(AM)=\operatorname{tr}(AN)=K\). The exact nonnegative Hilbert–Schmidt commutator energy gives \(\operatorname{tr}N\ge\operatorname{tr}M\), with equality exactly when \(AB=BA\). The two-eigenvalue power formula \(T^x=F_{1-x}(w)I+F_x(w)T\) reduces the entire parameter comparison to the monotonicity of \(\sinh(pw)/\sinh w\); the sign reverses exactly at \(2t=1\). Equal determinants turn trace comparisons into exact 2-by-2 log-majorization; strictness is proved. The local standard-library checker passed 896 exact rational assertions; it is not used to infer the continuum of inequalities.

originality.rationale: Ibrahim–Huang, arXiv:2610.23736v1, states the two comparisons explicitly as Conjecture 5.6, after proving only endpoint log-majorization, midpoint isospectrality, and a 2-by-2 matrix representation. Its material §4–5 was inspected and does not prove the all-parameter 2-by-2 conclusion or the equality cases. Earlier inspected spectral and Wasserstein-mean articles compare different pairs of curves. The 2025 near-geometric article remains an acknowledged full-text accessibility risk, but the accessible abstract predates the near-spectral construction; no decisive overlap was identified. Distinct nearby published results have different objects and do not imply the quantified statement.

value.rationale: This establishes the entire natural dimension-two case of the explicitly stated Conjecture 5.6, not a trivial specialization of an already proved general statement. It gives both directions for every continuous interpolation parameter, exact strictness iff the input matrices do not commute, and an explicit hyperbolic trace-difference formula. The 2x2 matrix cone is a canonical spectral model and an essential testing ground for the open higher-dimensional problem; the exact phase law distinguishes qualitative endpoint facts from genuine global behavior.
